claims.text: As-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr has a solidification-segregated dendritic microstructure.
The dendrites in as-cast WTaTiVZr are enriched in W and Ta.
The interdendritic regions in as-cast WTaTiVZr are enriched in Zr and Ti, with V distributed between the regions.
The segregated dendritic microstructure enhances plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
The W-Ta-rich regions strengthen the alloy through multicomponent solid-solution strengthening.
Lattice distortion and frictional resistance in the W-Ta-rich regions contribute to high strength.
The Zr-Ti-rich regions, assisted by V, lower the valence-electron concentration.
Ti, V, and Zr modify dislocation cores and facilitate localized plastic deformation.
The heterogeneous dendritic structure improves grain-boundary cohesion.
Localized plasticity and improved grain-boundary cohesion impede crack nucleation and propagation.
As-cast WTaTiVZr will have higher yield and ultimate strengths than powder-sintered pure tungsten at room and elevated temperatures.
As-cast WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten, particularly above 200 °C.
As-cast WTaTiVZr will have a lower brittle-to-ductile transition temperature than pure tungsten.
As-cast WTaTiVZr will show less scratch-induced cracking and chipping than pure tungsten.
The scratch-derived fracture toughness of WTaTiVZr will be well above 25 ± 1 MPa√m.
The comparison tungsten plate has coarse equiaxed grains of approximately 100 ± 20 µm.
The indentation-derived yield strength of the baseline tungsten is approximately 700 MPa at room temperature.
The indentation-derived yield strength of the baseline tungsten is approximately 250 MPa at 500 °C.
The baseline tungsten exhibits minimal plasticity below 300 °C.
The scratch-derived fracture toughness of the baseline tungsten is approximately 25 ± 1 MPa√m.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes the product as having a 'homogeneous but segregated microstructure,' whereas the other fields emphasize substantial compositional segregation into distinct dendritic and interdendritic regions. Homogeneity and segregation are not operationally reconciled.
